pr.title: Link the branch's Vercel preview rather than the head's own build
pr.head: 1011bfaff7521c594f5bab797ec2c186a424fd82

summary: Projector shows each pull request it watches in two places: the panel, a pane in Claude Code drawn by the hooks module in hooks/, and the console, a terminal view drawn by project console in Python. Each has a row model that turns the watch daemon's cached GitHub answer into a row and a drawer. Both models link the pull request's Vercel preview: open in vercel in the panel's drawer, and the d key in the console.

Until now that link went to the URL of one Vercel build, such as projector-l5ul8g3q0-okamnesiac.vercel.app. Every push makes a new one, so a tab opened from the link kept showing old code. Vercel also gives each branch a stable preview address that always serves the branch's newest ready build. This pull request links that address instead.

GitHub's deployment data carries only the per-build URL. The branch address appears only in the comment the vercel bot keeps on the pull request, whose first line is a Markdown link reference, [vc]: #<signature>:<base64 JSON>. The JSON lists each Vercel project with its previewUrl and nextCommitStatus. The address can't be built from the branch name, because Vercel shortens a long name with a hash.

Both row models now read the newest vercel comment from the comments(last:100) the daemon already fetches, so the GitHub query doesn't change. A successful Vercel build on the head still decides whether there is a link at all. When no comment names a usable branch address, the link falls back to the build's own URL.

cards.title: Which link a row gets
cards.html:
SituationLink
No successful vercel deployment on the headnone
Newest vercel comment lists a DEPLOYED project with a plain hosthttps://<host>
No such comment, unreadable metadata, or no usable projectthe build's URL

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Build preview: the URL of one Vercel deployment, fixed to one commit.
  • Branch preview: the address Vercel keeps per branch, which serves its newest ready build.
  • Row model: the code that turns the daemon's cached GitHub answer into a row, once in TypeScript for the panel and once in Python for the console.
  • Shared row fixtures: the cases under tests/fixtures/rows/ that both models must pass, so the two stay in step.

groups.title: Reading the branch preview in both row models
groups.kicker: The TypeScript and Python row models gain the same comment parser.
intro: Each model renames its old previewOf / preview_of, which read the head commit's deployments, to buildPreviewOf / build_preview_of. It adds a parser for Vercel's comment and a new previewOf / preview_of that combines the two.

The parser walks the pull request's comments newest first and skips any comment not written by the vercel bot. It also skips a comment whose metadata won't decode, and stops at the first one that does. In that comment it returns the first project whose nextCommitStatus is DEPLOYED and whose previewUrl is a bare host name. The host check keeps a crafted value from putting a different link into the drawer's Markdown.

checks.text: The two parsers agree: both anchor the [vc]: reference at the start of the body, use the same host pattern, go on to an older comment when decoding fails, and stop at the newest readable one. The shared fixture runs through both models, and claude plugin test . and the CI check job passed.

files.note: The panel's row model: the comment parser and the new previewOf, which toPullRequest now calls with the whole pull request node.

checks.text: The host must be letters, digits, and hyphens in two or more dot-separated labels, with no scheme, path, or spaces. Anything else is ignored and the build URL is used instead.
toReversed is an ES2023 array method, from the same library as the findLast that hooks/inbox.ts already compiles with. hooks/typecheck.sh could not run on the review runner.

files.note: The console's row model: the same parser in Python, with to_pull passing the node and the head commit.

checks.text: Vercel's base64 omits padding, so the code restores it before decoding. A decode or JSON failure raises a ValueError subclass, which sends the loop on to the next older comment.
Run against GitHub, rows.to_pull returned the branch hosts for #607, #606, and this pull request, while build_preview_of returned each one's per-build URL.

groups.title: The shared fixture case
groups.kicker: One new case covers four pull requests through both models.
intro: previews.ts holds four pull requests: several comments where only the newest vercel one counts and a person's look-alike is ignored; a failed head build, which gets no link; unusable projects (an injected link and a PENDING project), which fall back to the build; and unreadable metadata, which falls back too. index.ts registers the case for the panel's tests. The Python tests find it by globbing the fixture directory.

groups.title: Documentation
groups.kicker: The docs and the query's comment describe the new link.
intro: docs/plugins.md describes the drawer's open in vercel link and its fallback, and docs/cli.md describes the console's d key. The comment above the daemon's query in watch.py now says that the deployments decide whether Vercel built the head, and that the link comes from the bot's comment. The query itself is unchanged.

files.note: Comment only; the query is unchanged.
